brief: This week's list grew to 50 startups, with 31 joining for the first time. The strongest newcomer is Ayar Labs, an optical chip startup that raised $650 million this year to fix a data-movement bottleneck slowing down AI data centers. The trend of the week is private space infrastructure, as newcomers like The Exploration Company and MBRYONICS build the capsules, rockets and laser communication hardware that let governments and companies run their own space missions.
gaps: AI medical scribes like Nabla, Tandem Health and Voize all target doctors and nurses; nobody here builds the same speak-instead-of-type note automation for vets, dentists or mental health therapists, professions with the same paperwork burden and much less competition.

Space hardware builders like The Exploration Company, MBRYONICS, Kepler Aerospace and Open Cosmos are multiplying, but nobody insures the satellites and missions they launch; a Stoïk-style insurer built specifically for space assets and mission failure could pair naturally with this wave.

Cross-border fintechs like barq, Aspora, Ontop and Stream serve migrants, expats and gig workers, but none of them serve refugees or asylum seekers, who have similar cross-border money needs plus no credit history and often no bank account at all.

AI-for-science startups like AQEMIA, Cradle and Cubase Bio apply generative AI and physics to drugs and proteins; the same approach could be pointed at breeding new crop varieties faster, a natural extension for a company like xFarm that already has farm-level data but no molecular design layer.

AI legal tech is crowded with tools for lawyers and companies (Lawhive, Lexroom, Solve Intelligence, Summize, Magnar, netLex), but almost all of it serves English or Latin American markets; a similar AI legal assistant built for individuals navigating everyday legal problems in Middle Eastern or Southeast Asian legal systems is still missing.
run_line: 65 searches of 250, 94 pages of 200, 60 startups judged of 60, 48 minutes

title: Hot Startups

trends.name: AI legal tech
trends.sentence: A wave of startups are using AI to help lawyers and companies research law, draft documents, review contracts and manage legal work faster.

trends.name: AI shortcuts lab science
trends.sentence: Several startups pair generative AI with physics or biology simulation to design new drugs, proteins, materials or engineering products without years of trial-and-error lab work.

trends.name: Cross-border finance for underserved workers
trends.sentence: Fintechs are building banking, payroll and payment products specifically for migrants, expats, gig workers and hourly employees who traditional banks ignore.

trends.name: Private space infrastructure
trends.sentence: Startups are building the hardware for satellites, launch vehicles and optical communications that let governments and companies run their own space missions.

trends.name: AI medical scribes
trends.sentence: AI tools that listen to doctor-patient conversations and automatically write structured clinical notes are appearing across multiple countries to cut clinician paperwork.

trends.name: Cybersecurity gets specific
trends.sentence: Security startups are moving away from broad vulnerability scanning toward embedded, developer-first or exploitability-focused defenses that tell teams exactly what to fix.
